title: Idiosyncrasy Catalog — Labeling Diary
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy diary of weird labeling edge cases I keep hitting. For short-term reference and to sketch experiments before formalizing into the labeling guide. Notes-to-self tone.

High-level goals:
- Capture recurring oddities so we can create deterministic heuristics or abstain rules.
- Draft small regexes / sampling queries to find more examples.
- Prioritize items by impact (production downstream errors, eval regressions, high-frequency tokens).

Recent hits (examples):
1) SKU-like tokens that look like dates: 2021-07-10 vs PROD20210710A.
   - Problem: model/labeler conflates date entity vs product id.
   - Heuristic sketch: if token contains alpha prefix and >6 contiguous digits, mark as SKU; if strictly ISO-ish (YYYY-MM-DD) then date.
   - Quick regex prototypes: SKU: (?i)^[A-Z]{2,5}\d{6,}$ ; date-ish: ^\d{4}[-/]\d{2}[-/]\d{2}$
   - Ambiguity example: "INV2021-07-10" -> prefer SKU if alphabetic prefix present.

2) Hyphenation broken by OCR on invoices: linebreak-hyphenated words (e.g., "trans-\naction")
   - Many annotators treat as two tokens or join incorrectly.
   - Temporary rule: if a hyphen at line end followed by newline -> join without hyphen ("transaction"). If hyphen in middle of sentence -> preserve.
   - Note: preserve original text in provenance but normalize for labeling. Add flag: normalized_from_ocr=true.

3) Phone numbers with extensions and international noise: "+1 (415) 555-1212 x1234" or "0044 20 7946 0958 ext 100"
   - Decision: capture main number as PHONE, capture extension as PHONE_EXT when clearly separated by x/ext/extension. Create examples in label UI.

4) Abbrev collisions across languages: "Dr." (English title) vs "dr" (Dutch abbreviation for "de"?) and "S.A." in Spanish corp names vs sentence punctuation.
   - Policy: case-sensitive heuristics when available; fallback to context window (3 tokens) to decide. If preceding token is uppercase name, treat as title.

5) Email-like tokens inside hashes/fingerprints: "user+hash@service[.]com" or "foo at example dot com"
   - Heuristic: allow fuzzy matches for human-typed obfuscation; create separate label EMAIL_OBFUSCATED. Only mark as EMAIL if domain-like token after obfuscation rules apply.

Abstain rules I want to trial:
- If annotator confidence low OR token ambiguous by >2 heuristics, label as ABSTAIN.
- Specific triggers: < 5 visible alpha chars + mix of digits and punctuation (ambiguous id/date/amount), or single-token capitalized sequence of length 2-4 without context (could be initialism or part of product name).

Sampling queries to find candidate examples in prod dumps:
- tokens LIKE "%-%\n%" (linebreak-hyphenation)
- regex search: /[A-Z]{2,6}\d{6,}/ (SKU-like)
- phone-like strings with x|ext patterns search
Keep small sample of 500 per query for manual triage.

Short experiments to run (order):
1) Run SKU vs date regex sweep on last 7 days of logs, compute false positives on supervised set (use annotation s1).
2) Add OCR hyphen joiner pipeline and measure how many label diffs it causes on invoices. If >3% of tokens change label distribution, we need to include in data doc.
3) Add PHONE_EXT label to UI for one week; check inter-annotator agreement (target kappa > 0.75).

Labeler guidance snippets (for quick UI tiplines):
- "If a token has letters + >4 digits, prefer ID/SKU over date unless separated by clear date separators."
- "When you see hyphen+newline, join; when hyphen inside sentence, keep it."
- "Use ABSTAIN when unsure — we will adjudicate high-ambiguity clusters in batch."

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to reliably detect product SKUs that are 100% numeric but follow product name (e.g., "Widget 20210710")? (Suggest: look at left context; if token immediately follows known product token list, mark SKU.)
- Should we automatically normalize OCR punctuation (quotes, em-dash) before labeling or annotate on raw and normalize later? Pros/cons: normalizing reduces labeler cognitive load but hides provenance.
- Do we want to capture "obfuscation patterns" as metadata (e.g., obfuscated_email=true) or as explicit labels? My lean: both — label + metadata.

Quick notes from Slack and tickets:
- Slack: #labeling "Diego saw 120 mismatches on invoice OCR after new tesseract update" (link: slack://thread/CF12345)
- JIRA-2847: add SKU/dates split.

Adjudication heuristics (initial draft):
- Adjudicate by cluster: group ambiguous tokens by normalized form and top 3 conflicting labels, route top-30 clusters weekly to SMEs.
- Use majority vote unless votes split evenly, then SME.

Filenames & branches for experiments:
- grep queries & scripts: labeling-scripts/sku-date-sweep.sh
- branch: feature/sku-date-heuristics

Final: this is messy and intended as ephemeral. Once experiments above have results, distill into formal label guide section: "IDs vs dates", "OCR hyphenation", "phone + ext", "abstain policy".

If I return to this later:
- Put concrete examples (5-10 canonical examples each) into confluence page confluence:label-guides/v2#ids-vs-dates
- Add unit tests for regexes in labeling-scripts repo.

End of diary entry.

-- maya
